answer: Approval requires a commitment phase and an opening phase: signers first commit to their verdict hash, and only after the threshold is reached do they open, so a signer that changes its mind after seeing the tally cannot profit from the change. Each head pays its own cost, paid in full, since the cost is per identity. A farm locks a pigment before it can see the field, opens the trellis only after the threshold, and burns a copper if it tries to abstain between them: none of the three can be sequenced to the farm's advantage.
